usage:
hergy - run a team of agents on top of herdr

Usage: hergy <command> [options]

  up [definition]                      Start a team
  down [team|worker]                   Stop a team, or one of its workers
  status [team]                        Show how the members and workers are doing
  refresh <member>|--all               Restart a member
  reprompt <member>|--all              Send the bootstrap prompt again; the conversation stays
  apply [member]...                    Apply a changed definition to a running team
  focus <member>                       Move the focus to a member's pane
  nudge <member> [text]                Push an idle member to carry on
  stop <member>                        Interrupt a member's current turn
  tell <name> [text]                   Send a message to a member or worker
  hire <name>                          Add a worker
  turns [team]                         Watch a team and ask a member that stopped without handing on
  turn-done <team> <member> [payload]  Tell hergy a member's turn ended (the harness calls this)
  ls                                   List the team definitions
  show <definition>                    Show the final team definition and where each value came from
  new <definition>                     Write a starter team definition
  migrate                              Migrate legacy YAML definitions to Markdown rules
  validate                             Check the settings files
  serve                                Open the web UI in a browser
  version                              Show the version
  cheat                                Show the cheatsheet

Common options
  --dry                                Show what would happen, and do nothing
  --as <team>                          Run the same team definition under another team name (up only)
  --team <team>                        The team for apply, refresh, reprompt, hire, focus, nudge, stop and tell
  -C <dir>                             Use this directory as the project
  --lang en|ja                         Language of the command line (default en); the WebUI is Japanese
  --port <port>                        The port hergy serve listens on (default 8787)

Where team definitions live
  Project                              .hergy/teams/<definition>/team.yaml
  Outside the project                  ~/.config/hergy/teams/<definition>/team.yaml

Details of one command: hergy <command> --help

First steps
  hergy new myteam
  edit team.yaml
  hergy up myteam

hergy up [definition] [--as <team>] [--dry] [--json] [--timeout <ms>] [-C <dir>]
Boot the team definition in a new tab, with one pane and bootstrap prompt per member. The team name is trimmed before its shape is checked, both for --as and the screen.
"Sent" means herdr observed working within five seconds. Retry the identical prompt once on any sending error. If the final answer is agent_prompt_stalled, timeout or agent_blocked, name the recipient and pane, show how to send again, continue with the remaining recipients, and finish with failure listing the missing receipts. Other sending or startup failures stop the operation immediately. Only confirmed recipients get success lines.
If the agent asks a question while it starts (whether to trust this folder, for example), hergy names the member, the tab and the pane, waits for the answer with no limit, then sends the bootstrap prompt, confirms receipt and goes on; a second question in a row prints nothing more. Ctrl-C stops the wait, and the line it ends with names the way on. hergy answers nothing itself and moves no focus.
Refusal: a team named <team name> is already running; start it under another name
env is fixed when a pane is made. After editing env, run hergy down then hergy up. refresh keeps the pane and its env. Every pane hergy makes gets GY_ACTOR=<herdr name>; a profile's own GY_ACTOR does not win, and validate warns when a profile writes it.
Refusal: not received: <member> (pane <place>): <reason>
retry: <reprompt>
Refusal: cwd is not a directory: <place>; pass a directory to -C
Refusal: live agent names already in use: <herdr name>; run `hergy down`, then run this again
Refusal: run inside a Herdr-managed shell pane (HERDR_ENV=1 and HERDR_PANE_ID are required)

hergy down [team|worker] [--dry] [--json] [-C <dir>]
Close the panes of the running team's members and of the workers it hired. A team is what hergy made for it: the tab labelled with its name, and the panes named after it, "<team>-<member>". A pane whose agent ended, and one whose member never started (a boot stopped at a startup question), are closed too, so nothing hergy made is left; a pane hergy did not name is a person's own and stays. A name that is not a running team is looked for as one worker of a running team (its short name, or its herdr name "<team>-<worker>"): only that worker's pane is closed, and the worker's own tab when that pane was the last one in it; the members and the other workers stay.
After closing a team's panes, down waits up to 30000 ms in total for herdr to forget their names. A timeout fails and lists the remaining names. From a team pane, it waits for the other names before closing your own pane last; your own name cannot be awaited. On timeout it keeps your own pane open: run hergy down again after the names disappear. For a team, both the CLI and screen list remaining worktrees and clear its turn state, pending signals and tells on success or a name-release timeout; a timeout still fails. A screen stop also cancels this serve's pending start of that team. An empty team tab can be stopped by either entry point without closing the tab itself. The screen reports only member and worker panes actually closed; the watcher is excluded. Other errors stop before this cleanup. For one worker, down waits for herdr to forget its name before reporting success; a timeout fails, so a following hire does not reuse a name still held. A name that is both a team's and a worker's is refused, naming both.
After closing, it lists the git worktrees that came while the team was running (after the worker was hired, for one worker), other than the project root: an agent keeps its pane in the project root and cds into a worktree, so the pane's own directory is not enough to find them. The time comes from the launch record, and a worktree a closed pane stood in is marked. Each worktree comes with its branch, uncommitted changes and commits not in main, and the project's stashes, with the commands that remove them; hergy removes nothing, and temporary documents are not listed (hergy cannot tell which are the team's).
Refusal: run inside a Herdr-managed shell pane (HERDR_ENV=1 and HERDR_PANE_ID are required)

hergy status [team] [--json] [-C <dir>]
With a team name: one line per member and per worker, its live agent_status (working/idle/done/blocked), or "not running" when the member is not live; a worker carries "(worker)". Then a judgement line: "waiting for a human: <names>" when any is blocked, else "nobody is working" when none is working or blocked. With no team name: every running team, each with its team definition name, its member and worker counts, and the same judgement. It only reads herdr, and runs outside a herdr-managed pane too.

A member that is not live: start it again in the pane hergy named after it, when that pane is still at its shell. Every member a refresh starts starts with an empty conversation. The settings are read again first, so an edited kind, args or prompt takes effect.

Ctrl-C stops the wait, and the line it ends with names the way on. hergy answers nothing itself and moves no focus.

hergy apply [member]... [--team <team>] [--dry] [--json] [--timeout <ms>] [-C <dir>]
Compare the saved definition with the teams running from it and put each member right: send its prompt again when the prompt moved (the conversation stays), start a member the definition has and no agent is live for, or restart a member whose start (kind or args) changed (the conversation goes). Refused members are left, with the reason, and the rest go on; the command answers 1 while one is left, including with --dry or --dry --json. With no member named, every member with drift is applied. The screen removes duplicate recipients, reserves every team in a selection together, and cancels the entire apply when any of those teams is stopped. A startup failure reports the members that started, the panes left behind and the command to continue, just as a team start does. A worker's changed profile takes effect from the next worker.

hergy focus <member> [--team <team>] [-C <dir>]
Move the focus to a member's pane, by short member name or herdr name, so a person can answer it there. It changes nothing else.

hergy nudge <member> [text] [--team <team>] [--dry] [-C <dir>]
Send a member a short push to carry on. The text is headed by who it is from (the member whose pane you type in, else the human); with no text, a short "carry on".
Refusal: <member>: status "<status>"; a nudge is sent only when the agent is idle or done. Run it again then

hergy stop <member> [--team <team>] [--dry] [-C <dir>]
Send esc to a working member, ending its current turn and keeping its conversation. An idle or done member is left alone, and the command still succeeds: there is nothing to stop. Some agents need esc twice: the first only asks them to interrupt and they keep working. hergy watches the member's state after each esc and sends a second esc only while the member is still working, so an agent that stopped on the first is never sent a second (on some harnesses the second esc does something else). A member still working after two escs is reported as not stopped (exit 1), and refresh is named as the next step, the same step a real stop names. --dry prints what would stop and reads nothing.
Refusal: <member> runs in your own pane; a member cannot stop itself. Run it from another pane, or as the human

hergy tell <name> [text] [--from <member>] [--team <team>] [--dry] [-C <dir>]
Send a member or worker a message headed by who it is from. Both sender and recipient accept a short name or herdr name. --from names the sender; left out, it is the member or worker whose pane you type in, else the human. It does not check the recipient's state, so the message reaches an agent in any state. The tell is recorded for the team's watcher ($XDG_STATE_HOME/hergy/turns/<team>.tells/), which then knows who opened whose turn and who waits for whose answer. hergy tell human (人間, 外側, outside), typed in a member's or worker's pane or with --from, sends nothing and needs no text: it marks what they wrote in their pane as the person's, so the watcher does not ask who it is for when they stop; from a pane that is neither a member's nor a worker's it is refused.

hergy turns [team] [--log] [-C <dir>]
Watch one running team's turn (r-103d, r-378e). Members hand the turn on themselves with hergy tell; the watcher hands nothing on of its own. Once a second it takes the tells hergy tell recorded and the signals the members' harnesses wrote (hergy turn-done), and reads herdr. A turn ends when the harness says so (the signal, with the turn's last reply) or, for a member without a signal, when herdr sees the agent go from working to done or idle (then what it wrote in its pane during that turn is read); a wired member's stop waits up to 5 seconds for the signal; a signal for a stop already acted on is dropped. Who opened the turn decides what happens when it ends. A turn the outside opened (the person's hergy tell, the start prompt, hergy's own question) rests: the reply is the person's and nothing is sent. A turn another member opened (its hergy tell, or hergy delivering an answer; a worker's first turn: the member that hired it) that ends with a hergy tell in it was handed on by the member, and nothing more is done; one with hergy tell human in it is the person's: the turn goes to the human, those that waited wait no more, and nothing is asked. A tell that comes while the member works opens its next turn; when the turn then rests and no next turn begins within 10 seconds (a harness that folded the queued message into the running turn), that rested turn is taken as the answer and the member is asked about it. One that ends without a tell is asked about: the watcher sends the member "who is what you wrote for?" with the names it may answer (those waiting for it, then those the definition's turns name), human and nobody. The member's next stop is the answer: one name, and the text that waited is sent to that member with herdr agent prompt (one that is working gets it when it stops, as one message with everything that came meanwhile); human, nobody, no name or several leave the turn with the human, and the state says why. A member that stopped without writing a line while members waited, one hergy could not ask (blocked, or never started), or one whose recipient never started (no working state within 5 seconds, after one retry) also leaves the turn with the human. The same stop is acted on once. blocked is not a stop. Each line in the watcher's pane says how the end was seen: [signal: claude], [herdr saw the stop], or [no signal within 5 seconds; herdr saw the stop]; a delivery decided by an answer says [as answered]. The turn's state is $XDG_STATE_HOME/hergy/turns/<team>.json (holder, who opened whose turn, the question, the box); the tells wait in <team>.tells/ and the signals in <team>.signals/; hergy down removes all three. Its pane shows a three-line band redrawn in place: the team and each member's state (● working, ○ stopped, ◐ blocked), who holds the turn and from whom, who waits for whose answer; the latest handoffs with their time (→ handed, ✓ to the human, ? asked, ⟲ rested, ✗ not delivered or unclear); and what is being asked or boxed. The sentences (one per event, with how the end was seen) go to <team>.log with the time of each line; hergy turns <team> --log prints it, and hergy down leaves it. hergy up starts this in a four-row pane of the team's tab, and it ends when the pane closes.

hergy turn-done <team> <member> [payload]
What a member's harness calls when its turn ends (r-378e); a person does not type it. hergy up and hergy hire wire it into each start without writing into the person's own configuration: Claude Code gets --settings with a Stop hook (the person's hooks keep running), Codex gets -c notify=[hergy turn-done ...] (the person's own notify from ~/.codex/config.toml is called afterwards with the same JSON), and a --standalone opencode gets hergy's plugin directory ($XDG_STATE_HOME/hergy/opencode/hergy-turns) added to the plugins of OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (the profile's own inline config is kept; the person's ~/.config/opencode is read as before, which OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR would replace), with HERGY_BIN, HERGY_TEAM and HERGY_MEMBER in the pane's environment. A profile that passes --settings or notify itself, whose OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is not JSON, or that runs opencode without --standalone gets no signal, and hergy up says so; its stops are seen through herdr. The payload is Codex's one JSON argument (last-assistant-message) or, on stdin, Claude Code's Stop hook JSON (last_assistant_message) or the plugin's {"source":"opencode","last_assistant_message":...}. The signal is written for hergy turns to take.

hergy ls [-C <dir>]
List the visible team definitions and the running team names each one booted.

hergy show <definition> [-C <dir>]
Print the effective team definition and where each value and document came from.

hergy new <definition> [-C <dir>]
The starter members are lead and builder. Write team.yaml and agreement.md.
The members' roles and profiles are the ones either place already holds:
hergy writes no role document and no profile the person did not choose.
While neither place holds a role document, it writes the starter roles
lead and builder into roles/; while neither defines a profile, it writes
claude-default into profiles.yaml. Otherwise it names the roles and
profiles to write in team.yaml, and the next step is hergy validate.
An existing team is never overwritten. It writes into the project's .hergy/
inside a git repository, and into ~/.config/hergy/ outside one.
If the global config.yaml (version and lang) is missing, it is written too.

hergy migrate [--dry] [--global] [-C <dir>]
Inspect all legacy role and team YAML files in the project before writing. --global selects global settings, --dry only prints the plan. Keep adjacent .yaml.bak originals; refuse conflicting destinations. See CHANGELOG for recovery.

hergy validate [-C <dir>]
Check the global config.yaml, every profiles.yaml, and every team definition. Exit 1 if any is broken. It prints the size of each role document and team definition, each checked once. Each role and team has a provisional 1,200-character budget. A team's total includes rules plus fixed words in team/member prompt templates, excluding placeholders and generated text. Count Unicode code points, normalizing CRLF only for counting. Excess is a warning, never a startup failure.

hergy serve [--port <port>] [--no-open] [-C <dir>]
When renaming a role or profile with its usages selected, read every affected team definition and prepare all reference changes before writing. If any definition cannot be read or edited, refuse the whole save without changing files and name the definitions. Write the references first and rename the role or profile last. An I/O failure during writing returns failure and lists completed and unfinished writes; earlier writes are not rolled back. Renaming a role or profile in a project changes only that project's own definitions. A global rename checks the global definitions and every registered project's definitions, respecting a project's same-named role or profile.
Serve the screens over HTTP on 127.0.0.1, print the URL and open it in this machine's default browser, in the foreground, until Ctrl-C. --port picks the port (default 8787; 0 lets the operating system pick a free one); --no-open prints the URL and opens nothing. A browser that cannot be opened is one line on stderr and serve goes on, with the URL to open by hand. It reads the settings the way the commands do, and it changes nothing but the two profiles.yaml files (a profile's name, kind, args and env, and the profile each member and worker runs), a role document, a team definition's team.yaml and agreement.md, and the projects: list of the global config.yaml. It is the headquarters: it shows the projects config.yaml lists (or, without that key, the project it was started in and the global settings), their teams, roles and profiles with the project each belongs to, the running teams and workspaces, and it starts and stops a listed project's team with the same result as hergy up and hergy down. A stop waits for name release with the same 30000 ms deadline and reports any timeout in its result; if serve runs in a team pane, that pane stays open on timeout. A start runs in a workspace a person picks and reports its progress and a startup question at /api/hq/launches/<id>.
The listener accepts this machine only. Host must be 127.0.0.1 or localhost. A write is a POST, PUT or DELETE carrying this run's X-Hergy-Token. When Origin is sent, it must name the same server. The rendered page holds the token; read it there first.

hergy version
Print the commit and time of this hergy. It takes no other flags.

hergy cheat [--ai]
Print a cheatsheet. --ai prints this text. It reads only config.yaml, for the language, and prints even when that file is broken.

  -h, --help           Show this text

A team definition is a directory, teams/<definition>/ under .hergy/ or ~/.config/hergy/. A running
team has a team name: the team definition name by default, or another name given
to hergy up --as. Commands that read or write a team definition take a team
definition name (up, new, show); commands that act on a running team take a team

      version: 1        required, int; must be 1.
      lang: en|ja       string; the language when --lang is not given; default en.

Without the key, serve shows the project it was started in and the global settings. With an empty list it shows the global settings alone. A relative path is a broken setting that validate and serve refuse.

      version: 1        required, int; must be 1.
      description: "<text>" string, required; one line saying which case the team is meant for. A definition that writes none, or writes one over more than one line, does not read, and one that still writes the key it replaced is stopped with the sentence that says to write description: instead; hergy validate warns while it is still the starter example hergy new writes. The places a person picks or reads a definition read it (the team list, a definition's screen, the start sheet, hergy show); a team command's header and a running team's tiles do not, and it is never part of a member's prompt or of what hergy apply puts right.
      team: <definition> string, optional; if written it must equal the team definition name (the directory name).
      cwd: <dir>        string; working directory, relative to the project root; default ".".
      prompt: "<text>"  string, optional; the bootstrap prompt template for every member. It must keep %{role_doc} and %{docs}.
      members:          required, nonempty list.
        name: <member>     required, string; short member name matching [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}.
        role: <role>       required, string; a role name matching [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}; the name people read is the document's title. Reads roles/<role>.md (the project's first, then ~/.config/hergy/).
        profile: <name>    required, string; a named engine from profiles.yaml. kind, args and env are the profile's: writing one of them on a member is an error that says where it goes.
        cwd: <dir>         string; overrides the team cwd.
        prompt: "<text>"   string; overrides the team prompt. It must keep %{role_doc} and %{docs}.
      workers:          list, optional; which member may hire which worker. Each entry ties one worker to the member that hires it; the worker's two turns (the member to the worker, and the worker back) are made from it and cannot be written in turns:. A member and a purpose written twice is an error. A worker has one purpose: write two purposes as two entries (the same profile may be written twice), and a purpose with a comma or a Japanese comma stops the definition.
        - from: <member>     required, string; the member that hires this worker.
          purpose: <text>    required, string; what the worker is for; one purpose per worker, and one worker per member and purpose.
          profile: <profile> required, string; the engine that worker runs; a profile in profiles.yaml.

What stops it is a name that is no member and no human, a name written "<kind>:<name>" (no kind but human and a member may stand there yet), a turn to itself, the same turn twice, a member or the human that hands the turn to nobody, and no turn reaching the human. Arrows in rule text are not interpreted or compared with turns:.

Use Narrow or Wide in a column header, and Equal to reset the widths. Wide expands the selected document beyond the standard reading width. Apart from a column narrowed on purpose, no column is narrower than the standard reading width, and a wide column grows at twice the rate of the others; the board has its own horizontal scrollbar and an explanation when documents do not fit. roles/<role>.md and teams/<definition>/agreement.md hold complete Markdown text.
Saved text is inserted unchanged into %{role_doc} and %{docs}; placeholders inside rules are not expanded again.
The roster includes the short member name, the first-line title, role name, herdr contact and the self marker.
Arrows and role names in rules are not interpreted. Only team.yaml turns: controls topology validation.
The team screen edits the team document and distinct shared roles side by side, with one full-text field per file, heading outlines and block counts. Saving a shared role updates that file for every reader; stale saves are refused by file hash.
When renaming a role or profile with its usages selected, read every affected team definition and prepare all reference changes before writing. If any definition cannot be read or edited, refuse the whole save without changing files and name the definitions. Write the references first and rename the role or profile last. An I/O failure during writing returns failure and lists completed and unfinished writes; earlier writes are not rolled back. Renaming a role or profile in a project changes only that project's own definitions. A global rename checks the global definitions and every registered project's definitions, respecting a project's same-named role or profile.
A team definition copy writes team.yaml and writes agreement.md only if the source has it. A missing agreement is left absent at the destination; an unreadable agreement refuses the copy with its reason. A copy into the global place lists the role documents and profiles it does not hold, and writes only the ones the person chooses with the definition.
The delete confirmation counts readers of a global role or profile across every registered project. Definitions that cannot be read are not included in that count.
Each role and team has a provisional 1,200-character budget. A team's total includes rules plus fixed words in team/member prompt templates, excluding placeholders and generated text. Count Unicode code points, normalizing CRLF only for counting. Excess is a warning, never a startup failure.
There are no rule IDs, on/off fields or separate notes. Use hergy migrate --dry, then hergy migrate to convert legacy YAML explicitly, or add --global for global settings. Adjacent .yaml.bak files retain the original bytes, including excluded rules and notes. Old YAML at an active path stops validate and prompt generation. See CHANGELOG for collisions, symlinks, unsupported hard links and recovery.

herdr.guide_member:
- Hand your result, and what you need someone to do next, on with `hergy tell <name> "<text>"`, then stop. The name is the short one in the roster (lead, for example).
- Text for the person: write it in your own pane, hand it on with `hergy tell human`, then stop.
- If you stop without handing on, hergy asks who it is for. Answer with one name, "human" or "nobody".
- Do not use `herdr agent prompt`: hergy would lose whose turn it is.
- To add a teammate use `hergy hire`, not `herdr agent start`: a teammate started through herdr is missing from hergy's roster, down and status.
herdr.guide_worker:
- Hand your result on with `hergy tell <the member that hired you> "<text>"`, then stop. A question before you are done goes the same way.
- If you stop without handing on, hergy asks who it is for. Answer with one name.
- Do not use `herdr agent prompt`: hergy would lose whose turn it is.
- A worker adds no teammates: ask the member that hired you if another worker is needed.
